raw:
“I felt proud when I finished my first quilt for my niece. The corners lined up evenly—that’s one of the things I remember best. You look at the whole quilt, but then your eye goes to where the pieces meet. I was pleased with that.

“And I’d stitched her initials into one square. That little square made it hers, not just a quilt I’d finished. When I think about it, I go back to those initials, and then the corners again. I’d actually finished something for her, and I was proud of how it turned out.”
